objective: Define canonical host request and result envelopes for tree-draft inference.
mathematical_spec: Let R=(request_id,session_id,input_tokens,sampling,limits,metadata) and O=(request_id,status,accepted_tokens,output_tokens,usage,finish_reason). Require request_id uniqueness over live requests and O.request_id=R.request_id.
implementation_prompt: Specify plain host-side request/result structs with explicit token spans, sampling parameters, limits, metadata ownership, and finish status. Keep the contract backend-neutral and suitable for C, C++, Python, IPC, HTTP, and gRPC adapters.

objective: Specify the request lifecycle state machine used by every API surface.
mathematical_spec: States S={created,queued,running,streaming,completed,cancelled,failed}. Legal transitions are created->queued->running, running->streaming, and queued|running|streaming->completed|cancelled|failed; terminal states have no outgoing transitions.
implementation_prompt: Define a deterministic lifecycle state enum and transition validator. State changes must be monotonic, thread-safe at the contract level, and reusable by host, Python, IPC, HTTP, and gRPC layers.

objective: Define a stable cross-language error taxonomy and error payload.
mathematical_spec: E=(domain,code,message,retryable,request_id,details). Map internal failures into finite domains {invalid_argument,resource_exhausted,cancelled,deadline,unavailable,internal,protocol}. Equal causes must map to equal domain/code pairs.
implementation_prompt: Specify stable error codes and a structured error record with no transport-specific fields. Include retryability and optional request correlation while preserving a deterministic mapping from engine errors.

objective: Specify buffer ownership and allocator hooks for the C boundary.
mathematical_spec: For every exported buffer b, owner(b) is exactly one of caller,library,shared. Transfer operations must preserve unique ownership; release(release(b)) is invalid and release(NULL) is a no-op.
implementation_prompt: Define C-compatible byte/token span types, allocator callbacks, release rules, and ownership annotations. Avoid hidden allocation conventions and make every returned buffer releasable through an explicit API.

objective: Define ABI versioning and feature negotiation for native bindings.
mathematical_spec: Represent ABI version as V=(major,minor). Compatibility holds iff major_client=major_lib and minor_client<=minor_lib. Feature set F is a bitset intersected as F_eff=F_client & F_lib.
implementation_prompt: Specify exported ABI version queries, feature bits, struct-size fields, and forward-compatible initialization rules so older clients can detect compatibility before creating runtime objects.

objective: Specify opaque C handles for runtime, session, and request objects.
mathematical_spec: Let H be opaque nonzero handles with generation g. A handle is valid iff allocated(h,g) and not released(h,g); every successful retain increments refcount and every release decrements it to zero exactly once.
implementation_prompt: Define opaque handle types and create/retain/release semantics for runtime, session, and request objects. Specify invalid-handle behavior and thread-safety expectations without exposing C++ layout.

objective: Specify callback-based native streaming for token and terminal events.
mathematical_spec: For request q emit ordered events e_i with sequence i starting at 0. Exactly one terminal event T occurs; no event may follow T. Token payload order must equal engine commit order.
implementation_prompt: Define a C callback signature carrying sequence number, token delta, usage delta, and terminal/error information. State reentrancy and callback lifetime rules and forbid callbacks after terminal delivery.

objective: Define a C++ RAII facade over the stable C ABI.
mathematical_spec: For each wrapper W(h), destructor(W) performs exactly one release(h) unless ownership moved. Move transfers h and nulls source; copy is disabled unless backed by retain/release.
implementation_prompt: Specify thin C++ classes for runtime, session, request, and stream subscription that own C handles with RAII and preserve the C ABI behavior without adding independent runtime state.

objective: Define configuration validation and normalization at API entry.
mathematical_spec: Let C_raw map keys to values and N(C_raw)=C canonical. Validation V(C) returns either C or a finite set of field errors. N must be idempotent: N(N(C))=N(C).
implementation_prompt: Specify validation for model/runtime limits, speculative parameters, sampling settings, transport limits, and batching fields. Return structured field errors and deterministic defaults.

objective: Specify cooperative cancellation shared by all frontends.
mathematical_spec: Cancellation token c is monotonic: 0->1 only. If cancel(q) wins before terminal(q), terminal(q)=cancelled; if terminal already exists, cancel is idempotent and cannot change it.
implementation_prompt: Define cancellation token semantics, request cancellation entry points, and race behavior between cancellation and normal completion. Keep cancellation cooperative and observable across thread and transport boundaries.

objective: Specify request deadlines and timeout semantics.
mathematical_spec: For monotonic clock t, deadline d is expired iff t>=d. Effective deadline d_eff=min(d_request,d_transport,d_session) over defined values. Expiry before terminal produces deadline error exactly once.
implementation_prompt: Define absolute monotonic deadlines and optional relative timeout conversion at ingress. Specify propagation into scheduler work and mapping to cancellation without relying on wall-clock time.

objective: Define credit-based backpressure for streaming consumers.
mathematical_spec: Let c>=0 be outstanding credits and each emitted chunk cost w_i>=1. Emission is legal iff c>=w_i; after emit c:=c-w_i and after grant(k), c:=c+k. Producer memory must remain bounded when c=0.
implementation_prompt: Specify a transport-neutral credit window for streamed token chunks. Define grant, consume, pause, resume, and cancellation behavior so slow consumers cannot cause unbounded buffering.

objective: Specify the bounded host event queue between engine and adapters.
mathematical_spec: For capacity K, queue size n satisfies 0<=n<=K. Events preserve per-request FIFO order. Enqueue on full queue either blocks through backpressure or returns resource_exhausted according to configured mode.
implementation_prompt: Define a bounded multi-producer event queue contract with per-request ordering and explicit full-queue behavior. Keep queue semantics independent of any one network transport.

objective: Define admission control for request batching.
mathematical_spec: For request q with estimated cost c(q), admit set B such that sum c(q)<=C_budget and |B|<=B_max. Rejected admission returns resource_exhausted or remains queued according to policy.
implementation_prompt: Specify admission metadata and decisions for max batch size, token budget, queue depth, and per-request cost estimates. Expose enough status for frontends without embedding scheduler policy.

objective: Define session identifiers and lifecycle semantics.
mathematical_spec: A session s has state {open,closing,closed}, unique id u, and generation g. New requests require state=open. close(s) is idempotent and no request may attach after transition to closing.
implementation_prompt: Specify session create/get/close operations, stable IDs, optional client-provided keys, generation handling, and terminal behavior for in-flight requests during graceful versus forced close.

objective: Specify API-visible session context binding to engine state.
mathematical_spec: Map M: session_id -> engine_context_ref is injective for simultaneously live session generations. Bind/unbind operations must be atomic with session lifecycle transitions and never expose raw engine pointers.
implementation_prompt: Define the host contract that associates a session with internal KV/speculative state while preserving opaque ownership. Include attach, lookup, detach, and stale-generation rejection.

objective: Define the request submission contract from APIs to the scheduler.
mathematical_spec: submit(R) returns handle h or error before execution. For accepted requests, exactly one scheduler ticket exists, carrying request_id, session binding, priority, deadline, and estimated cost.
implementation_prompt: Specify an adapter-neutral submission interface that translates validated requests into scheduler tickets. Include synchronous admission result and asynchronous terminal completion.

objective: Specify deterministic event sequencing and terminal delivery.
mathematical_spec: For each q, sequence numbers are contiguous 0..N and terminal event has sequence N. Let committed token deltas D_i concatenate to output O; concat(D_0..D_{N-1})=O with no duplication.
implementation_prompt: Define event sequence assignment, token delta grouping, usage updates, finish reasons, and exactly-once terminal publication so every binding can reconstruct the same result.

objective: Define transport-neutral metrics names and accounting rules.
mathematical_spec: Counters are monotonic integers; gauges are instantaneous; histograms observe nonnegative durations/sizes. Request accounting satisfies accepted=completed+cancelled+failed+inflight over a consistent snapshot.
implementation_prompt: Specify metric identifiers, labels with bounded cardinality, units, and update points for queueing, batching, token throughput, speculative acceptance, latency, cancellation, and errors.

objective: Define trace context propagation across host and transport layers.
mathematical_spec: Trace context T=(trace_id,span_id,flags,baggage). Child spans preserve trace_id and generate unique span_id. Invalid external context is dropped rather than partially trusted.
implementation_prompt: Specify trace context fields in host metadata, ingress extraction, scheduler propagation, streaming span events, and terminal status mapping without coupling to one tracing SDK.

objective: Define structured logging correlation and redaction semantics.
mathematical_spec: Every request log record L includes timestamp,level,event,request_id and optional session_id/trace_id. Sensitive token/text fields are excluded by default; enabled payload logging must be explicit and bounded.
implementation_prompt: Specify structured event names and correlation fields for API lifecycle logs. Define a redaction policy and prohibit high-cardinality or prompt-content logging by default.

objective: Define the pybind11 module surface over the native C++ facade.
mathematical_spec: Python objects P wrap RAII objects W with a one-to-one live ownership relation unless explicitly shared. Destruction of P releases W once; module import exposes a version compatible with native ABI negotiation.
implementation_prompt: Specify pybind11-exposed Runtime, Session, RequestHandle, result/error enums, and version query. Keep methods thin wrappers around the C++ facade and document ownership.

objective: Define Python-native request/config conversion rules.
mathematical_spec: Let f map Python dict/dataclass input to canonical C++ request C. For valid x, normalize_python(x) followed by f must equal host normalization N(f(x)); unknown fields fail deterministically.
implementation_prompt: Specify Python dataclasses or typed objects for request, sampling, limits, usage, and results. Define conversion, defaults, validation errors, and integer/range checks.

objective: Specify Python future-style unary completion.
mathematical_spec: A Python RequestFuture resolves exactly once to result or exception. cancel() delegates to native cancellation. done() is monotonic false->true and callbacks execute after resolution.
implementation_prompt: Define a Python awaitable/future wrapper for non-streaming requests, including thread-safe result delivery, cancellation races, deadline errors, and interpreter shutdown behavior.

objective: Specify Python asynchronous iteration for streaming tokens.
mathematical_spec: For async iterator A, each __anext__ returns the next ordered event or raises StopAsyncIteration after one terminal success; terminal failure raises mapped exception once, then iteration remains closed.
implementation_prompt: Define an async iterator binding backed by the native event stream. Integrate credit grants with consumer progress and preserve exact event ordering without busy polling.

objective: Define Python cancellation propagation for tasks and generators.
mathematical_spec: If asyncio task cancellation occurs while native request q is live, invoke cancel(q) once. Native cancelled terminal maps to asyncio cancellation semantics without double terminal delivery.
implementation_prompt: Specify hooks that translate Python task/generator cancellation into the native cancellation token and cleanly detach callbacks during interpreter or event-loop shutdown.

objective: Define GIL ownership and native callback threading rules.
mathematical_spec: Potentially blocking native calls execute with GIL released. Any transition into Python code requires GIL held. No native mutex may be held while acquiring GIL if that mutex can be reached from Python reentry.
implementation_prompt: Specify where pybind11 releases/acquires the GIL for submission, waits, callbacks, and stream delivery. State lock-order rules to prevent deadlock and allow concurrent inference.

objective: Specify zero-copy Python views for immutable token/binary buffers.
mathematical_spec: A Python view v may alias native buffer b iff lifetime(v)<=lifetime(b) through shared ownership and b is immutable while exported. Otherwise copy. Shape/stride metadata must describe exact bytes.
implementation_prompt: Define optional memoryview/buffer-protocol exposure for token arrays and binary IPC payloads with shared lifetime guards. Fall back to copying when alignment or mutability constraints fail.

objective: Define deterministic native-to-Python exception mapping.
mathematical_spec: Mapping M(error.domain,error.code)->ExceptionClass is total for known errors and falls back to RuntimeError-like internal exception. Preserve code, retryable, request_id, and details as attributes.
implementation_prompt: Specify Python exception hierarchy and pybind11 translators for validation, cancellation, deadline, resource exhaustion, unavailable, protocol, and internal errors.

objective: Define a length-delimited IPC frame format for local or remote workers.
mathematical_spec: Frame F=(magic,version,type,flags,stream_id,payload_len,payload,checksum?). Require payload_len<=L_max and decoder consumption exactly header+payload. Unknown mandatory frame types are protocol errors.
implementation_prompt: Specify endian-stable IPC frame fields, message types, maximum sizes, incremental decoding, and malformed-frame rejection. Use an envelope that can multiplex requests and stream events.

objective: Define IPC handshake, ABI compatibility, and capability negotiation.
mathematical_spec: Peers exchange H=(protocol_major,protocol_minor,features,max_frame). Connection is usable iff majors match; negotiated minor=min(minors), features=intersection, max_frame=min(maxima).
implementation_prompt: Specify hello/ack handshake messages, authentication placeholder fields if needed, timeout behavior, and explicit failure reason before any inference request is accepted.

objective: Specify shared-memory payload descriptors for large IPC buffers.
mathematical_spec: Descriptor D=(region_id,offset,length,access,generation). Valid iff 0<=offset, 0<=length, offset+length<=region_size and generation matches. Receiver must never dereference stale generation.
implementation_prompt: Define an optional shared-memory descriptor message and ownership protocol for large token/logit buffers, including region registration, reference lifetime, bounds checks, and fallback to inline payloads.

objective: Define IPC flow-control credits and bounded send queues.
mathematical_spec: Per stream j maintain credit c_j and queue bytes q_j<=Q_max. Sending frame of size s requires c_j>=s; then c_j:=c_j-s. CREDIT(k) increases c_j by k up to configured cap.
implementation_prompt: Specify per-stream byte credits, connection-wide queue limits, credit update frames, fairness expectations, and behavior when peers stop granting credit.

objective: Specify multiplexing of concurrent requests over one IPC connection.
mathematical_spec: Each live request maps to unique stream_id. Frames for a stream preserve sequence order while frames across streams may interleave. stream_id cannot be reused until terminal acknowledgement or connection epoch changes.
implementation_prompt: Define stream ID allocation, request/open frames, event frames, terminal frames, and demultiplexing state. Include connection epoch handling to prevent stale-frame confusion.

objective: Specify IPC cancellation propagation and acknowledgement.
mathematical_spec: CANCEL(stream_id) is idempotent. Receiver maps it to cancel(q). Exactly one terminal frame follows if the stream was live; unknown already-terminal stream IDs may return an idempotent cancel acknowledgement.
implementation_prompt: Define cancel and cancel-ack frames, races with terminal events, and sender behavior so disconnect or user cancellation cannot produce duplicate terminal state.

objective: Define IPC disconnect, crash, and reconnection semantics.
mathematical_spec: On connection loss epoch e, every nonterminal remote request in e transitions to unavailable unless explicitly resumable. New connection uses epoch e+1 and cannot deliver old frames into new request state.
implementation_prompt: Specify how host adapters fail in-flight requests on worker disconnect, clear multiplexing state, reject stale shared-memory generations, and expose retryability without automatic unsafe replay.

objective: Define the HTTP endpoint and JSON schema surface for inference.
mathematical_spec: HTTP request J maps deterministically to canonical host request R. JSON numeric/string bounds are validated before submission. Response JSON derives only from canonical result/error fields.
implementation_prompt: Specify versioned HTTP routes for health, models/runtime info, inference, streaming, sessions, and cancellation. Define content types, required fields, limits, and request correlation headers.

objective: Specify translation from OpenAI-compatible completion/chat requests into host requests.
mathematical_spec: Translator T maps supported OpenAI fields to R. For unsupported field x, behavior is explicit reject or ignore-by-contract. Token limit relation must satisfy effective_max=min(client_max,server_max).
implementation_prompt: Define field mappings for model, prompt/messages after upstream tokenization contract, temperature, top_p, top_k extension, stop, seed, max tokens, stream, user metadata, and speculative options via namespaced extension.

objective: Specify translation from canonical results/events to OpenAI-compatible responses.
mathematical_spec: Unary response U and streamed chunks C_i must reconstruct the same generated token/text sequence and finish_reason. Usage totals in terminal response equal canonical usage counters.
implementation_prompt: Define OpenAI-compatible completion/chat response shapes, IDs, choices, finish reasons, usage, error envelope, and extension fields without leaking internal engine pointers or unstable enums.

objective: Define Server-Sent Events encoding for streamed inference.
mathematical_spec: Each SSE event encodes one logical chunk as UTF-8 data lines terminated by blank line. Event order equals canonical sequence order. Terminal success emits final chunk then [DONE] exactly once.
implementation_prompt: Specify SSE event formatting, JSON chunk boundaries, keepalive comments, terminal [DONE], error event behavior, and buffering constraints compatible with incremental HTTP flushing.

objective: Specify SSE disconnect detection and backpressure coupling.
mathematical_spec: Let writable window w be transport capacity. Grant host stream credits only when w permits flush. Client disconnect triggers cancel(q) unless request policy explicitly permits detached completion.
implementation_prompt: Define integration between HTTP socket writability, host stream credits, cancellation on disconnect, keepalive scheduling, and bounded pending bytes.

objective: Define HTTP status and error-envelope mapping.
mathematical_spec: Map invalid_argument->400, cancelled->499 or configured client-close semantics, deadline->504, resource_exhausted->429/503 by cause, unavailable->503, protocol->400, internal->500. Body retains stable error code.
implementation_prompt: Specify deterministic HTTP status mapping and an OpenAI-compatible error body with stable internal code, message, type/domain, request ID, and retry hints where appropriate.

objective: Define gRPC service and message contracts for unary and session operations.
mathematical_spec: Protobuf messages must represent canonical R/O/E without lossy field conversion. Field numbers are never reused; unknown fields are preserved by normal protobuf compatibility semantics.
implementation_prompt: Specify proto service methods and messages for Infer, session create/close, cancel, runtime info, and health. Reserve field numbers for evolution and use explicit enums for stable statuses.

objective: Specify gRPC server-streaming semantics for token events.
mathematical_spec: For stream q, gRPC messages carry canonical sequence i and preserve order. One terminal status ends the RPC; no application event follows terminal. Flow control gates host credit grants.
implementation_prompt: Define the server-streaming RPC payload for token deltas, usage updates, finish reason, and structured error metadata. Couple HTTP/2 flow control to the host backpressure contract.

objective: Specify gRPC deadline and cancellation propagation.
mathematical_spec: Effective deadline is min(host request deadline,gRPC context deadline). gRPC cancellation sets native token once. Native deadline/cancel terminal maps to canonical gRPC status without duplicate completion.
implementation_prompt: Define ingress extraction of gRPC deadlines, context cancellation callbacks, native cancellation invocation, and status/detail mapping for races between peer cancellation and engine completion.

objective: Define transport-aware dynamic batching metadata normalization.
mathematical_spec: For every ingress request q, adapter emits batching tuple B(q)=(compat_key,priority,deadline,cost,streaming). Requests may batch only when compat_key equal and scheduler constraints permit.
implementation_prompt: Specify how HTTP/OpenAI, gRPC, Python, and IPC adapters populate common batching metadata so batching policy receives equivalent information regardless of transport.

objective: Define consistent session lifecycle operations across Python, HTTP, gRPC, and IPC.
mathematical_spec: All transports implement the same abstract operations create(s), submit(s,q), close(s,mode). For a session generation, ordering is linearizable with respect to create/close boundaries.
implementation_prompt: Specify adapter mappings for session IDs, optional client keys, graceful/forced close, stale session errors, and reconnect behavior so transport choice cannot change core session semantics.

objective: Define observability exposure and propagation at public API boundaries.
mathematical_spec: Metrics endpoint exports schema from ID_319; trace headers map to ID_320; logs use ID_321 correlation. Cardinality constraints exclude raw request/session IDs from metric labels.
implementation_prompt: Specify HTTP metrics/health exposure, gRPC interceptors, Python hooks, IPC correlation fields, and trace/log propagation. Keep observability optional and behaviorally inert when disabled.

objective: Define cross-binding conformance vectors for request, stream, error, and cancellation semantics.
mathematical_spec: Given canonical vector v, each binding adapter A_i must satisfy decode_i(encode_i(v))=v for supported fields. Event traces must be equivalent after transport framing is removed.
implementation_prompt: Specify a language-neutral corpus of valid/invalid requests, expected normalized forms, event sequences, errors, cancellation races, deadline cases, and session transitions for later implementation tests.

objective: Specify the end-to-end Pilar G integration contract and invariants.
mathematical_spec: For every accepted request q across binding b, canonical normalization, lifecycle, ordered token output, terminal status, usage, cancellation, and error code must be observationally equivalent modulo transport framing. Resource buffers and handles reach zero live ownership after terminal teardown.
implementation_prompt: Define the final integration checklist and adapter interface boundaries tying native API, Python, IPC, HTTP/OpenAI/SSE, and gRPC to one canonical host contract. State invariants required before implementation can be considered complete.
